# Pixel art: every character's close-up portrait (ready-to-paste ChatGPT prompts)

<!-- Generated by tools/pixel/portrait_prompts.py from tools/pixel/portrait_cast.json and the style block and expressions in docs/pixel-art-brief.md. Don't edit by hand: change those and run the tool. -->

A front-facing, chest-up pixel portrait for every character with a personal quest or real dialogue: the companions, the main story, the villains and bosses who speak, and the named supporting cast. They're the faces in the dialogue box and in cutscene close-ups (`docs/pixel-art-brief.md` §4). The player and {sb} aren't here: their faces are the layered kit (brief §4.6, `docs/pixel-art-batch-1.md` §2).

**How to use it.** Each character has a file here. Open it, start a **new chat** in ChatGPT, attach the template it names (in `tools/source/pixel/templates/`), and paste the first block whole. Then stay in the **same chat** and paste each block after it in order, one message each, saving each picture under the name in the block's last line. Staying in one chat keeps the face, the pixels and the framing the same in every expression. If a picture comes back wrong, use a fix below and do it again.

**The whole list in one file:** [ALL-PORTRAITS-for-ChatGPT.md](ALL-PORTRAITS-for-ChatGPT.md). Upload it to ChatGPT with both templates, and say "next" for each picture. It has the same prompts as the character files, with the rules written once. Start a new chat every character or two: long chats drift.

**Where the files go.** `tools/source/pixel/portraits/<id>/`, one folder per character (a variant's pictures go in its character's folder).

**What to send Claude.** A character's whole set at a time. Claude snaps each picture to a true 96 × 96 pixel grid, cleans the palette, and animates it (blinking, talking, breathing, the expression changes, brief §4.3). Brannock's set is the pilot (batch 1): send his first, in case the prompts need a change, then the companions, then the rest in the order below.

Expressions by tier (brief §4.2): **main** all 13; **named** 8 (neutral, angry, disgust, smile, laugh, sad, shock, worried); **minor** 6 (neutral and the five: angry, disgust, smile, laugh, sad). A missing one falls back to the nearest, so a set works before it's finished.

**69 characters, 686 pictures.**

## Fix the size (use when a picture comes back wrong)

```text
That came back the wrong size or moved. Do it again, and give it back at exactly 1024 by 1024 pixels, with the character exactly where the grey mannequin is in the template: the eyes on the dashed eye line either side of the centre line, the chin on the chin line, the shoulders filling the bottom edge, the face looking straight at the viewer. Don't crop, zoom, turn, re-centre or re-frame it. Everything else stays exactly as it was.
```

## Fix the pixels (use when a picture comes back smooth or with tiny pixels)

```text
That looks too smooth and detailed. Redo it as real low-resolution pixel art: a grid of about 96 by 96 big square pixels, each about 10 to 11 image pixels wide and one flat colour, with no blending between them, a small palette, and a one-pixel dark brown-violet outline. Keep the character, the expression, the size and the position exactly the same.
```

## Fix the face (use when an expression changed who it is)

```text
That changed the character's face, hair or clothes. Go back to the neutral portrait and change ONLY the expression this time: the same person, the same hair, clothes, colours, pixels, size and position, still looking straight at the viewer.
```

### In the game (2026-11-25)

Every front-facing source saved so far is converted and in the dialogue box (53 portraits, counting variants): `python tools/pixel/portrait_kit.py build` turns them into `Content/Portraits/<id>.png` (one 96 x 96 face per expression, a 32-colour palette per portrait) and `review` draws contact sheets in `shots/pixel/portraits/`. After saving new pictures, run `build <id>` for that character and `python tools/check_assets.py`. Valencia uses the black-hair-red-eyes redesign. Brisk has only neutral and angry so far; his other lines fall back to the nearest face until #424 on are painted.
